sources.finding: The current REST catalog lists dependency review, submission and SBOM operations. It documents no dependency-graph configuration GET. No undocumented endpoint was queried.

The repository read documents admin visibility for security_and_analysis. The current owner/admin response includes that block but no dependency_graph configuration field; absence of a field does not establish feature state.
Public repositories are described as on by default. Repository administrators are described as able to enable or disable the graph.

The repository procedure uses Settings > Security and quality > Advanced Security and an Enable action beside Dependency Graph. It also describes a Disable action and enable/disable management regardless of repository visibility.

This page describes dependency graph as permanently enabled for public repositories. That conflicts with the enabling procedure and with this authenticated public-repository configuration observation.

The feature-availability section describes dependency graph as not enabled by default and as available for all repositories with administrator enable/disable control. Its default-state wording differs from the dependency-graph concept page.

The legacy GET exports SPDX dependency data, not a configuration flag. Documented status meanings are 200 OK, 403 Forbidden and 404 Resource not found, without a unique disabled-state interpretation. The page announces legacy export closing after 2026-11-13 and an asynchronous generation/fetch flow; generation was not requested.

documentationReconciliation.repositorySpecificConclusion: The current owner/admin Settings row takes precedence for this repository-specific configuration question. It shows an Enable action, so disabled is verified despite generic public-repository default/permanent-enable statements. This does not settle why those documentation statements differ, whether they describe a rollout, or how SBOM population will behave after a future authorized change.
